fact_sheet.business_description: Alithe Company operates a broad digital-commerce ecosystem serving consumers, merchants, and enterprises through marketplaces, cloud computing, and logistics [D01]. It functions as a platform that earns fees and marketing revenue by facilitating trade without owning all underlying merchandise [D01].

Cloud computing, international commerce, and other initiatives: various initiatives [D01]
unit_economics: High cash generation; operating cash flow of RMB 231.786 billion in fiscal 2021 [D02]
Non-GAAP free cash flow of RMB 172.662 billion [D02]
Capital intensity varies by segment; commerce engine is established and cash-generative, while new businesses require ongoing reinvestment [D01, D02]
competitive_position: Network effects, data, merchant relationships, and infrastructure provide genuine competitive advantages [D01]
Dominant scale with approximately one billion annual active consumers globally [D01]

final.memo:
The Company operates a dominant digital-commerce ecosystem, serving approximately one billion active consumers through its marketplaces, cloud computing, and logistics infrastructure [D01]. Historically, the business has generated massive free cash flow, reporting RMB 172.662 billion in fiscal 2021, and holds a strong balance sheet with over RMB 473 billion in cash and short-term investments [D02]. While it possesses the scale and network effects we admire, our investment mandate requires simple, predictable businesses free from extrinsic factors we cannot control [D01, D05].

The opportunity, which appears as a 38.9% drawdown from recent highs, is marred by mounting regulatory and policy interventions [D03, D04]. The market is currently pricing in existential risks, including antitrust fines and the potential for the structural invalidation of the variable-interest-entity (VIE) structures used by offshore investors [D01, D02, D04]. We cannot distinguish between a temporary market overreaction and a permanent impairment of the firm's business model, as we lack the ability to influence or predict the path of government policy [D01, D04, D05].

Given the lack of regulatory clarity, we cannot confidently project the earnings growth algorithm or an appropriate terminal multiple for this business [D01]. While the stock trades at 19.6x adjusted EPS, the risk of a near-total loss of equity value in the bear case—due to the potential unenforceability of the VIE structure—precludes us from viewing this as an attractive investment at current levels [D03, D04]. We do not invest in businesses where the governance model is fundamentally at odds with the rights of our investors [D01, D05].

We pass on this investment because it is hostage to extrinsic factors, specifically government policy and legal structure, which are outside of our control [D05]. Our process requires us to identify specific catalysts to unlock value, yet here, the regulatory environment is in flux with no clear resolution path [D01, D04]. Consequently, we have decided to avoid this exposure entirely, as the current risk profile is inconsistent with our standards for durable, high-quality compounding [D05].
